question: A Cisco UCS C-Series server is installed at a data center. The server should be managed by the Cisco UCS Manager by using a single cable for management and data traffic. Which configuration should be applied after the physical connection is established?
options:
UCS-A# scope server 1
UCS-A /server# scope cimc
UCS-A /server/cimc # scope mgmt-conn sideband
UCS-A /server/cimc # mgmt-conn-state enabled
UCS-A /server/cimc/mgmt-conn* # commit-buffer

UCS-A# scope chassis 1
UCS-A /chassis# scope cimc
UCS-A /chassis/cimc # scope mgmt-conn sideband
UCS-A /chassis/cimc/mgmt-conn # mgmt-conn-state enabled
UCS-A /chassis/cimc/mgmt-conn* # commit-buffer

UCS-A# scope chassis 1
UCS-A /chassis# scope cimc
UCS-A /chassis/cimc # set mgmt-conn-state enabled
UCS-A /chassis/cimc/mgmt-conn* # commit-buffer

UCS-A# scope server 1
UCS-A /server# scope cimc
UCS-A /server/cimc # scope mgmt-conn sideband
UCS-A /server/cimc/mgmt-conn #set mgmt-conn-state enabled
UCS-A /server/cimc/mgmt-conn* # commit-buffer
theory: Single-connect (sideband) management of a C-Series server lets Cisco IMC management traffic ride the same cable as data traffic, rather than requiring a dedicated management link. To enable it in the CLI you scope to the server object itself (not the chassis, since a standalone/integrated C-Series server isn't addressed as a chassis) and then scope into its CIMC's management-connection settings — 'scope server 1' > 'scope cimc' > 'scope mgmt-conn sideband' — before enabling the connection state and committing. Using the chassis scope instead targets the wrong managed object for a rack server. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 12 — Cisco UCS C-Series Integration, Sideband Management)
